purpose: Define remediation as explicit candidate changes linked to quality failures, with validation, provenance, authorization and re-evaluation before acceptance.

topics.name: DWH Quality Remediation Workflow
topics.purpose: Define remediation as explicit candidate changes linked to quality failures, with validation, provenance, authorization and re-evaluation before acceptance.

semantics.candidate_rule: Remediation proposal is inert candidate data until explicit apply.
semantics.source_rule: Candidate references exact failing quality result and source revision.
semantics.mutation_rule: Correction uses normal DWH mutation/transaction contracts.
semantics.automation_rule: Automated repair is allowed only through an explicit bounded remediation rule/operation profile.
semantics.conflict_rule: If source revision changed since failure, remediation enters concurrency conflict handling.
semantics.history_rule: Original failure and pre-remediation revision remain traceable.
semantics.success_rule: A successful write is not equivalent to successful remediation until required revalidation passes.

invariants.rule: Data-quality rules and results produce explicit evidence about exact data/schema identities; they never silently rewrite source data, change semantic ownership, declassify content or become authorization decisions.

hard_gates.condition: remediation applies to stale revision without conflict check
successful write assumed quality pass without revalidation

references.purpose: Stale remediation cannot overwrite newer state.
AI/tool remediation suggestions remain inert until governed apply.
